headline: Habagat Cancels Clark-Masbate Flights, PBA Games and Intramuros Visits
deck: Two Cebgo flights, a PBA doubleheader and visits to major Intramuros attractions were canceled or postponed on Sunday amid persistent monsoon rain.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Persistent southwest monsoon rain disrupted flights, professional basketball games and visits to historic sites on August 9. Cebgo canceled flights DG6171 from Clark to Masbate and DG6172 from Masbate to Clark, according to a list updated by GMA News at 11 a.m.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: The canceled outbound Clark-Masbate flight affected 42 passengers, while 71 passengers were affected on the return leg.
The Philippine Basketball Association postponed its Phoenix-versus-Rain or Shine and Barangay Ginebra-versus-Blackwater games. The league said a revised schedule would be announced.
The Intramuros Administration temporarily closed Fort Santiago, Baluarte de San Diego, Casa Manila Museum and Museo de Intramuros and canceled scheduled events because of the weather.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: The southwest monsoon, locally called the habagat, had brought persistent rain and flooding risks across parts of Luzon, prompting agencies and event organizers to revise operations for public safety.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The PBA had not announced replacement dates, and Intramuros reopening details were not yet final at publication time. Airline disruption lists can change, so the two flights in this report should not be treated as a complete list for the rest of the day.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The disruptions affect passengers, ticket holders and visitors across transport, sports and tourism. Current advisories help people avoid unnecessary travel during severe weather.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: Passengers should confirm flight status directly with their airline before traveling. PBA ticket holders and Intramuros visitors should monitor the organizations' official channels for replacement schedules and reopening notices.
